newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish spy for Moscow to be freed next July.
newsitem.headline: Swedish spy for Moscow to be freed next July.

text.p: Swedish spy Stig Bergling, who leaked his country's defence plans to the Soviet Union, will be conditionally set free next July after serving half his sentence, penal authorities said on Thursday.
Bergling, once a senior officer in the Swedish security police, was jailed for life in 1979 for spying for Moscow but the sentence was commuted to 23 years.
Some defence experts say he was in a position to have revealed virtually all Sweden's defence plans.
Bergling made a sensational escape in 1987 by absconding from an unguarded house where he had asked to pay a conjugal visit to his wife.
He was a fugitive abroad for seven years before unexpectedly giving himself up to police in 1994 when he was again imprisoned.
A year ago, Bergling appealed for clemency saying he was suffering from Parkinson's disease.
Birgitta Guntsch, a member of Sweden's KVN penal authority, said the decision to free Bergling next July 16, halfway through the 23-year sentence and taking account of his escape, had been unanimous.
"There is no significant risk of a relapse into similar criminality," she said.
But Krister Thelin, an opposition conservative member of the authority, who opposed leniency for Bergling, did not take part in the decision.
"My basic view is that crimes of this type do not indicate any remission of half-sentence," Thelin told the news agency TT.
